### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **44** documentable anchor(s).

**37** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d0c377beb988b990e77aa4763fd5e4b429d8de4`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `userId (5 routes)`
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d0c377beb988b990e77aa4763fd5e4b429d8de4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5a6fcc3f437d60e891c01188b01c74e89b4b3053` — the merge of head `5c0974f9e7ad8b9bef9b1a7261e1d65ed4e814c9` into base `0d0c377beb988b990e77aa4763fd5e4b429d8de4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5a6fcc3f437d60e891c01188b01c74e89b4b3053 && git checkout 5a6fcc3f437d60e891c01188b01c74e89b4b3053
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0d0c377beb988b990e77aa4763fd5e4b429d8de4 5c0974f9e7ad8b9bef9b1a7261e1d65ed4e814c9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0d0c377beb988b990e77aa4763fd5e4b429d8de4 && git merge --no-ff 5c0974f9e7ad8b9bef9b1a7261e1d65ed4e814c9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d0c377beb988b990e77aa4763fd5e4b429d8de4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0d0c377beb988b990e77aa4763fd5e4b429d8de4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

domain:server#6 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5p3T5YWhLjurajudnQ

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `2aeb9e05f8037a63cc7dc768d15cee6cff20b7fd`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration. The committed tree touches no `packages/spec/src/**` and no governed path. The `.changeset/` and `content/docs/**` files are prose surfaces. The review is owed only because of the `Clause-②: yes` line, so the tier is `TIER_DEFAULT`. Inputs read: card #30924 (its body and all 8 comments, including the PR 1 report 6686260557, the hand-off 6688338299 naming rulings 1A/3/4/5, claim 6710542762 and dev report 6712181248), the body and 12-file list of PR #31249, the net diff `origin/main...2aeb9e05`, and the 47 check-runs on the head.

Check-runs on `2aeb9e05` when read: 19 success, 12 skipped, 16 in progress, 0 failed. Among the green ones: Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · ESLint, Type Check · source gates, Dogfood Regression Gate, Spec property liveness. This record judges the contract only; the in-progress gates still have to read green before ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

Published reach: both packages export only `.` (plugin-auth also `./rate-limit-storage` and `./client-address`). plugin-auth's `index.ts` runs `export * from './auth-session-audit.js'` and exports `AuthManager`. plugin-audit's `index.ts` exports `createAuthEventAuditSink` and the types `AuthSessionAuditEvent`, `AuthEventAuditSink` and `AuthEventAuditSinkOptions`.

1. **plugin-audit `AuthSessionAuditEvent.userId`: `string` becomes optional. Right.** For the caller the accept-set widens (an event may leave out `userId`). For an implementer or reader `userId` is now possibly undefined: a new obligation, not a narrowing. `recordAuthEvent` is declared with method syntax, so its parameter is checked bivariantly and an existing annotated implementation still type-checks. The only in-repo implementer, `createAuthEventAuditSink`, is updated. At runtime a subject-less `login_failed` is now written with `user_id`, `record_id` and `actor` null; every other subject-less event still writes nothing (ablation B2). The row falls in `isLedgerRowAboutNoRecord`, served under the ledger grant; with a null `tenant_id` only the platform administrator sees it. `user_id`, `record_id` and `actor` are `required: false` on `sys_audit_log`.
2. **plugin-auth `AuthEventAuditSurface.recordAuthEvent` event `userId?`, and the derived `AuthSessionAuditEventInput`. Right.** Same analysis as item 1. At runtime it fails safe: `emitAuthSessionAuditEvent` swallows what a sink throws, so an older sink (including an older plugin-audit with a newer plugin-auth) loses only the subject-less rows. `audit-service.mdx` now shows `userId?` and says when it is absent. No value accepted before is refused now.
3. **New public `AuthManager.resolveRefusedSignInAccountId(email)`. Right.** Additive widening of an exported class, an in-process lookup, the forwarder ruled Q1-A; no new reachable type.
4. **Exported `signInFailureEventFor` now returns `null` for `reason: 'IP_NOT_ALLOWED'`. Right in-repo; disclosure incomplete.** Its accepted input and declared return type (`| null`) are unchanged; what shrinks is the set of events it produces, so no `(narrowing)` arm is owed. In-repo `IP_NOT_ALLOWED` reaches the after-hook only from the organization door, which now writes the richer row; without the suppression there would be two rows (ablation A4). An out-of-repo host mapping outcomes through this helper would silently lose that row: the PR body says so under Acceptance notes, the changeset does not. Should-fix S1.
5. **New module `ip-allow-list-refusal-audit.ts`. Right.** No subpath or entry type graph reaches it; `auditAllowListRefusal` is private. Nothing new is published.
6. **Row data contract seen by cloud#3668. Right.** `login_failed` rows now carry `metadata.rule: 'ip_allow_list'`, `metadata.attempts`, `metadata.reason: 'IP_NOT_ALLOWED'`, plus `tenant_id` when an organization's list refused. Free-form `context` keys, no schema change, no new error code.
7. **Behaviour against the card and its rulings. Right.** Deployment gate rows on `/sign-in/*` only (ruling 4); a row even when no account resolves (ruling 1A); organization door writes on session creation only, a refused switch writes none (Q2-A); bound 1st/10th/100th per address per 10 minutes, cap 1000 per window with one warn line, tracked addresses capped (ruling 5, Q3-A). The detached body read and lookup keep the 403's status, body and timing independent of whether the account exists (150 ms lookup case, ablation A6). No credential reaches a row. Both doors resolve the same `audit` object, so they share one bound. Sign-in runs with no native transaction, so a row written before the throw is not rolled back.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset level is right.** `patch` for `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `Metadata-protocol: none` (nothing an author writes changes). Both declaration lines start a line in the PR body and in the changeset; Check Changeset is green.
- **Declared arm `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right.** The diff widens published accept-sets (items 1, 2) and the public surface (item 3) and narrows no published accept-set: the implementer burden in items 1–2 comes from widening the input domain and does not break assignment; item 4 shrinks what a helper produces, not what it accepts. No BREAKING banner, migration or ADR-0087 marker is owed. Matches claim 6710542762 and forecast 6685098880.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report 6712181248: `open_questions` empty. PR 1's three open questions (6686260557) were ruled in 6688338299 and this diff follows each (Q1-A item 3; Q2-A pinned by A3; Q3-A pinned by the bound tests).
- **Out-of-scope 1 (class a, public door `POST /api/v1/auth/sign-in/email`). Escalated.** An organization-list `IP_NOT_ALLOWED` refusal counts toward the ADR-0069 D2 lockout with the right password (`auth-manager-after-hook.ts` passes any returned APIError to `recordSignInOutcome(email, false)`). Pre-existing on `main`, outside this card's surface, not blocking this contract; this PR leaves the counting as it was (the lockout path still writes `account_locked`; only the duplicate `login_failed` is suppressed). The seat files it before ACCEPT; that card's fix keys on the same refusal code and must keep `REFUSALS_RECORDED_AT_THEIR_DOOR`.
- Out-of-scope 2, the exact-60-minute flake: #31175 carries it. Nothing owed.
- Residuals declared and accepted as ruled: per-process bound (N replicas, up to N times the rows); the deployment row is written detached after the 403, so a runtime ending right after responding can lose it; only a JSON `email` names an account at the deployment gate.
- Not blocking: the organization-list row is pinned through `AuthManager.handleRequest` with a sink double plus plugin-audit's own unit case; the dogfood pin covers only the deployment list.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-v9d4f2`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5p3T5YWhLjurajudnQ`

**VERDICT: PASS**

Should-fix S1 (relayed to the dev): the changeset should also say that the exported `signInFailureEventFor` now answers `null` for `reason: 'IP_NOT_ALLOWED'` (the refusing door writes that row), and that a sink registered on the `audit` slot now receives `login_failed` events with no `userId`. Out-of-scope 1 is filed as #31251.
